readmeExcerpt:
OpenSRE: The open-source agent for CI/CD reliability

Your CI tells you it broke, but not why or how to fix it. OpenSRE is a CLI agent that reads the failed run, traces the cause and pushes a fix for you to review. Self-hosted, with your own models.

Quickstart · Docs · FAQ · Security

--- > 🚧 Public Alpha: Core workflows are usable for early exploration, though not yet fully stable. The project is in active development, and APIs and integrations may evolve. --- ## Before you begin Make sure you have: - A terminal open in a code project - A Git repository (recommended for the full workflow demonstration) ## Step 1: Install and start opensre macOS or Linux: ```bash curl -fsSL https://install.opensre.com | bash -s -- -gh ``` Windows (PowerShell): ```powershell & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://install.opensre.com/install.ps1))) -gh ``` Then start OpenSRE: ```bash opensre ``` Windows details: [Windows](docs/install/windows-local.mdx). The installer fetches the latest build from `main` without requiring sudo. If `opensre` is not found, follow the PATH instructions printed by the installer or open a new terminal. For supported platforms and troubleshooting, see [Install locally](https://www.opensre.com/docs/install/install-local). --- ## Table of Contents - [Before you begin](#before-you-begin) - [Install and start opensre](#step-1-install-and-start-opensre) - [Why OpenSRE?](#why-opensre) - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Deployment](#deployment) - [How OpenSRE Works](#how-opensre-works) - [Integrations](#integrations) - [Security](#security) - [Telemetry](#telemetry) - [License](#license) - [Citations](#citations) --- ## Why OpenSRE? AI writes more of the code every month. Someone still has to fix the build. When CI goes red, it tells you _that_ something failed, not _why_ or how to fix it. Under deadline pressure, teams hit re-run and move on, flaky checks pile up, `main` stays red, and the real investigation waits for whichever senior engineer has time. OpenSRE is an open-source CI/CD reliability agent that does that investigation for you, built to run on your own infrastructure with your own models: - **Recover from red builds faster:** it investigates the moment a run fails, reading logs, testing hypotheses and pushing a fix for you to review - **Fix the cause, not just the rerun:** it separates CI-caused failures from code-caused ones, so you fix the right thing - **Know what CI is costing you:** failure rate, developer hours lost to unreliable CI, and how long `main` stays red - **Senior-level context for everyone:** every engineer gets the same depth of analysis SWE-bench1 showed that agents improve fastest with realistic tasks and clear feedback. Pipeline failures are slower, noisier and harder to reproduce than local code tasks, so we hold OpenSRE to the same standard by: - running real-world end-to-end tests across cloud-backed scenarios [(tests/e2e)](tests/e2e) - keeping semantic test-catalog naming so e2e vs unit and local vs cloud boundaries stay obvious [(tests/README.md)](tests/README.md) Start with the **[CI/CD overview](docs/cicd/overview.mdx)**: analyze a repository's CI reliability, fix failing checks on a PR, or set up an agent that keeps CI green. 1 https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06770 --- ## Quick Start Contributors: start at [`main.py`](main.py) for the process entrypoint map. Run `opensre` to sign in and get started. The first launch activates the hosted model. ```bash opensre ``` Webapp contributors can run `opensre setup --dev` to authenticate through `http://localhost:3000`. **Interactive shell** — with no subcommand, `opensre` validates your account and starts a REPL (TTY required). You can exit and stay signed out, but the shell only opens for an active account. Describe incidents in plain language, watch the agent work, and use slash commands for session control (`/help`, `/status`, `/cost`, `/sessions`, `/resume`, `/compact`, `/new`, `/exit`) and integrations (`/integrations list`, `/integrations verify`). Ctrl+C cancels an in-flight turn without losing session state. See **[interactive shell commands](https://www.opensre.com/docs/getting-started/interactive-shell-commands)** for the full reference. **Headless CLI** — run one agent turn non-interactively from a terminal, script, or CI job: ```bash opensre ask "why is checkout-api slow?" ``` See **[Headless CLI](https://www.opensre.com/docs/guides/headless-cli)** for stdin prompts, JSON output, and tool approvals. **From Python** — drive the agent in-process from your own code (source checkout required): ```python from surfaces.embedded import start_embedded_session session = start_embedded_session() result = session.chat("why is checkout-api slow?") # ``answered`` is true for any reply text, including a failed model call. # That failure sets accounting_status to "not_run" and stop_reason to "error". if result.action_result.accounting_status == "completed" and not result.cancelled: print(result.primary_response_text) ``` See **[Python API](https://www.opensre.com/docs/guides/python-api)** for sessions, conversations, and custom output sinks. **For your team's daily loop:** embed OpenSRE in the Python services and automations your teammates already use. Start with the in-repo [Python API guide](docs/guides/python-api.mdx), then use it every day to make incident response repeatable. Other useful commands: ```bash opensre integrations setup opensre update opensre uninstall # remove opensre and all local data ``` --- ## Deployment An OpenSRE Cloud managed gateway, an AWS EC2 path, and a general self-hosted option: - **OpenSRE Cloud managed gateway:** an organization admin provisions it in the web app; signed-in shell users can check, start, or stop it without handling infrastructure credentials locally. - **Gateway (AMI + systemd):** `make build-gateway-image` then `make deploy-gateway` — Telegram gateway only, no Docker; the gateway is installed into a server image that new servers start from. - **Self-hosted container (Railway / ECS / Vercel):** deploy the repo `Dockerfile`, select `MODE`, and set `LLM_PROVIDER` plus its API key. Use `DATABASE_URL` only when the gateway needs shared Postgres-backed state, such as Slack Events API replicas. **[Full deployment steps and prerequisites → DEPLOYMENT.md](DEPLOYMENT.md)** --- ## How OpenSRE Works When a CI run fails, an alert arrives, or you ask a question, OpenSRE automatically: 1. **Fetches** the relevant context: failing checks and CI logs, recent commits and deploys, and correlated logs, metrics and traces 2. **Masks** sensitive identifiers (optional) before external LLM calls 3. **Reasons** across your connected systems to test hypotheses in a tool-calling loop, separating CI-caused failures from code-caused ones 4. **Answers** with an evidence-linked response in the conversation 5. **Fixes** the cause and pushes it to the PR branch for you to review, or suggests next steps and, optionally, executes remediation actions 6. **Posts** a summary directly to Slack, PagerDuty, or Telegram — no context switching needed For the current code-level agent architecture after removing the old graph and chain framework layers, see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). --- ## Integrations OpenSRE connects to 60+ tools and services across the modern cloud stack, from LLM providers and observability platforms to infrastructure, databases, and incident management. | Category | Integrations | Roadmap | | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **AI / LLM Providers** | Anthropic · OpenAI · OpenAI Codex · Ollama · Google Gemini · OpenRouter · TrustedRouter · NVIDIA NIM · Bedrock
readmeHtml:
OpenSRE: The open-source agent for CI/CD reliability

Your CI tells you it broke, but not why or how to fix it. OpenSRE is a CLI agent that reads the failed run, traces the cause and pushes a fix for you to review. Self-hosted, with your own models.

Quickstart · Docs · FAQ · Security

🚧 Public Alpha: Core workflows are usable for early exploration, though not yet fully stable. The project is in active development, and APIs and integrations may evolve.

Before you begin

Make sure you have:

  • A terminal open in a code project
  • A Git repository (recommended for the full workflow demonstration)

Step 1: Install and start opensre

macOS or Linux:

curl -fsSL https://install.opensre.com | bash -s -- -gh

Windows (PowerShell):

& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://install.opensre.com/install.ps1))) -gh

Then start OpenSRE:

opensre

Windows details: Windows.

The installer fetches the latest build from main without requiring sudo. If opensre is not found, follow the PATH instructions printed by the installer or open a new terminal.

For supported platforms and troubleshooting, see Install locally.

Table of Contents

  • Before you begin
  • Install and start opensre
  • Why OpenSRE?
  • Quick Start
  • Deployment
  • How OpenSRE Works
  • Integrations
  • Security
  • Telemetry
  • License
  • Citations

Why OpenSRE?

AI writes more of the code every month. Someone still has to fix the build.

When CI goes red, it tells you that something failed, not why or how to fix it. Under deadline pressure, teams hit re-run and move on, flaky checks pile up, main stays red, and the real investigation waits for whichever senior engineer has time. OpenSRE is an open-source CI/CD reliability agent that does that investigation for you, built to run on your own infrastructure with your own models:

  • Recover from red builds faster: it investigates the moment a run fails, reading logs, testing hypotheses and pushing a fix for you to review
  • Fix the cause, not just the rerun: it separates CI-caused failures from code-caused ones, so you fix the right thing
  • Know what CI is costing you: failure rate, developer hours lost to unreliable CI, and how long main stays red
  • Senior-level context for everyone: every engineer gets the same depth of analysis

SWE-bench1 showed that agents improve fastest with realistic tasks and clear feedback. Pipeline failures are slower, noisier and harder to reproduce than local code tasks, so we hold OpenSRE to the same standard by:

  • running real-world end-to-end tests across cloud-backed scenarios (tests/e2e)
  • keeping semantic test-catalog naming so e2e vs unit and local vs cloud boundaries stay obvious (tests/README.md)

Start with the CI/CD overview: analyze a repository's CI reliability, fix failing checks on a PR, or set up an agent that keeps CI green.

1 https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06770

Quick Start

Contributors: start at main.py for the process entrypoint map.

Run opensre to sign in and get started. The first launch activates the hosted model.

opensre

Webapp contributors can run opensre setup --dev to authenticate through http://localhost:3000.

Interactive shell — with no subcommand, opensre validates your account and starts a REPL (TTY required). You can exit and stay signed out, but the shell only opens for an active account. Describe incidents in plain language, watch the agent work, and use slash commands for session control (/help, /status, /cost, /sessions, /resume, /compact, /new, /exit) and integrations (/integrations list, /integrations verify). Ctrl+C cancels an in-flight turn without losing session state. See interactive shell commands for the full reference.

Headless CLI — run one agent turn non-interactively from a terminal, script, or CI job:

opensre ask "why is checkout-api slow?"

See Headless CLI for stdin prompts, JSON output, and tool approvals.

From Python — drive the agent in-process from your own code (source checkout required):

from surfaces.embedded import start_embedded_session

session = start_embedded_session()
result = session.chat("why is checkout-api slow?")
# ``answered`` is true for any reply text, including a failed model call.
# That failure sets accounting_status to "not_run" and stop_reason to "error".
if result.action_result.accounting_status == "completed" and not result.cancelled:
    print(result.primary_response_text)

See Python API for sessions, conversations, and custom output sinks.

For your team's daily loop: embed OpenSRE in the Python services and automations your teammates already use. Start with the in-repo Python API guide, then use it every day to make incident response repeatable.

Other useful commands:

opensre integrations setup
opensre update
opensre uninstall   # remove opensre and all local data

Deployment

An OpenSRE Cloud managed gateway, an AWS EC2 path, and a general self-hosted option:

  • OpenSRE Cloud managed gateway: an organization admin provisions it in the web app; signed-in shell users can check, start, or stop it without handling infrastructure credentials locally.
  • Gateway (AMI + systemd): make build-gateway-image then make deploy-gateway — Telegram gateway only, no Docker; the gateway is installed into a server image that new servers start from.
  • Self-hosted container (Railway / ECS / Vercel): deploy the repo Dockerfile, select MODE, and set LLM_PROVIDER plus its API key. Use DATABASE_URL only when the gateway needs shared Postgres-backed state, such as Slack Events API replicas.

Full deployment steps and prerequisites → DEPLOYMENT.md

How OpenSRE Works

When a CI run fails, an alert arrives, or you ask a question, OpenSRE automatically:

  1. Fetches the relevant context: failing checks and CI logs, recent commits and deploys, and correlated logs, metrics and traces
  2. Masks sensitive identifiers (optional) before external LLM calls
  3. Reasons across your connected systems to test hypotheses in a tool-calling loop, separating CI-caused failures from code-caused ones
  4. Answers with an evidence-linked response in the conversation
  5. Fixes the cause and pushes it to the PR branch for you to review, or suggests next steps and, optionally, executes remediation actions
  6. Posts a summary directly to Slack, PagerDuty, or Telegram — no context switching needed

For the current code-level agent architecture after removing the old graph and chain framework layers, see AGENTS.md.

Integrations

OpenSRE connects to 60+ tools and services across the modern cloud stack, from LLM providers and observability platforms to infrastructure, databases, and incident management.

Category Integrations Roadmap
AI / LLM Providers Anthropic · OpenAI · OpenAI Codex · Ollama · Google Gemini · OpenRouter · TrustedRouter · NVIDIA NIM · Bedrock
Observability Grafana (Loki · Mimir · Tempo · annotations) · Datadog · Honeycomb · Coralogix · groundcover · CloudWatch · Sentry · Elasticsearch · Better Stack · Splunk · Victoria Logs · SignOz · OpenObserve · OpenSearch · Azure Monitor · New Relic
Infrastructure Kubernetes · AWS (S3 · Lambda · EKS · EC2 · CloudTrail · Bedrock) · Azure · ArgoCD · Helm
Database MongoDB · ClickHouse · PostgreSQL · MySQL · MariaDB · MongoDB Atlas · Azure SQL · Snowflake · Redis · RDS · Supabase · Neon
Data Platform Apache Airflow · Apache Kafka · Prefect · RabbitMQ · Dagster · Temporal
Dev Tools GitHub · GitHub MCP · Bitbucket · GitLab · Jenkins
Incident Management PagerDuty · Jira · Alertmanager · incident.io · ServiceNow · Trello (client helpers only) Linear
Communication Slack · Google Docs · Discord · Telegram · Rocket.Chat · WhatsApp · Buzz Notion · Teams · Confluence
Agent Deployment Vercel · EC2 · ECS · Railway
Protocols MCP

OpenSRE is community-built. Looking for a safe first contribution? Browse good first issue tickets or see the Good First Issues guide. See CONTRIBUTING.md for the full workflow.

Local environment: SETUP.md (all platforms, Windows, MCP).

Developing in this repo: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md (install from source, CI parity checks, dev container, deployment detail, telemetry reference).

Thanks goes to these amazing people:

Security

OpenSRE is designed with production environments in mind: structured and auditable LLM prompts, local transcript handling by default, and no silent bulk export of raw logs. See SECURITY.md for responsible disclosure.

Telemetry

First-party product analytics and Sentry (errors) are opt-out. Quick disable:

export OPENSRE_NO_TELEMETRY=1

Full matrix, DSN override, and local event logging → docs/DEVELOPMENT.md

License

Apache 2.0 — see LICENSE.

Citations

1 https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06770

aiSummary.oneLiner: Self‑hosted AI agent that diagnoses CI/CD failures and auto‑generates PR fixes
aiSummary.whatItDoes: OpenSRE watches a CI run, extracts logs, commits, and correlated telemetry when a build turns red. It masks sensitive data then feeds the context to a locally hosted LLM to run a tool‑calling loop that formulates hypotheses and validates them against integrated services such as Datadog, Grafana, and GitLab. The agent distinguishes CI‑induced failures from code defects, produces an evidence‑linked answer, and optionally creates a remediation pull request. Results are posted back to Slack, PagerDuty, or Telegram, keeping the incident in the same workflow. All components run without external SaaS dependencies, allowing teams to keep models and data on‑premise.
keyFeatures: Installation: One‑line curl installer fetches the latest binary without sudo.
Interactive REPL: TTY shell with slash commands for session control and integration verification.
Headless CLI: Single‑turn commands (opensre ask) suitable for scripting in CI pipelines.
Python API: In‑process session object (start_embedded_session) for custom automation.
Multi‑tool integration: Connects to 60+ services (Datadog, Grafana, Slack, PagerDuty, GitLab, etc.) via unified tool‑calling framework.
Automated PR generation: After root‑cause analysis, agent creates a fix branch and opens a pull request for review.
Sensitive data masking: Optional redaction of identifiers before any LLM request.

useCases.title: CI Engineer on‑call
useCases.description: When a nightly build fails, the engineer runs opensre to automatically pinpoint the failing test, retrieve relevant logs, and generate a corrective PR, reducing mean‑time‑to‑recovery from hours to minutes.

useCases.title: Automation pipeline
useCases.description: A CI/CD script invokes opensre ask to diagnose flaky tests during the pipeline, captures the analysis as JSON, and aborts the run only if the failure is code‑related, preventing unnecessary reruns.

useCases.title: DevOps team with strict data policies
useCases.description: Because OpenSRE runs on self‑hosted infrastructure and masks secrets before LLM calls, teams can comply with internal security requirements while still leveraging AI‑driven incident analysis.

useCases.title: Platform reliability service
useCases.description: A SaaS provider embeds the Python API into its monitoring service to continuously scan customer repositories, automatically create remediation PRs for recurring CI failures, and surface cost metrics to product managers.

useCases.title: Incident response coordinator
useCases.description: The coordinator configures Slack integration so that every analysis and suggested fix is posted directly to the incident channel, eliminating context‑switching.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: OpenSRE is aimed at SREs, CI engineers, and DevOps teams that manage large codebases with frequent CI failures. It assumes familiarity with Git, a supported LLM provider, and access to the CI system’s API. Users should be comfortable running a terminal REPL or integrating Python packages into existing automation.
